newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr dips in late Tokyo, supported near 113.35 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr dips in late Tokyo, supported near 113.35 yen.

text.p: *Dollar dips in late Tokyo as speculative sales from U.S. funds through Singapore triggered stop-loss selling near 113.50-60 yen and then 113.40 yen, dealers said.
*Dollar fell as low as 113.35 yen before bids from Japanese operators emerged, allowing greenback to partly recover.

*News that parties in outgoing Japanese coalition had set up loose alliance and agreed on policy platform may have sparked dollar sales by removing overseas operators' worries about Japanese government stability, but long-term impact of this expected to be slight, one European bank dealer said.
*Dollar was down against yen in late Tokyo on Thursday, lacking momentum after spending most of afternoon virtually motionless.

*Profit-taking sales from U.S. funds above 114.00 yen kept top heavy, while bids from Japanese investors and importers, particularly oil companies, provided solid floor for greenback near 113.70 yen, dealers said.
*Dealers noted that investors appeared to be placing bids at 113.50 yen but warned that some stop-loss selling orders appeared to be lined up there as well.
